developing_opinions.stance: The gap between demo magic and operational reality is widening — most tools optimize for impressive demos rather than daily utility
Finally reaching the point where they're practical for real work, not just demos — but governance remains unsolved
Self-generating skills are mostly marketing theater — operational value comes from well-designed, bounded capabilities
The demo-to-deployment gap is especially pronounced in BaaS — platforms excel at prototyping but struggle with production concerns like data migration, vendor lock-in, and scaling costs
The problem is deeper than subscription creep — it's about cost visibility blindness. Teams can't manage what they can't see, and subscription models are designed to hide true costs
The real value isn't in tracking itself but in revealing systematic blind spots — teams consistently underestimate costs by 40-60% because subscription models obscure true operational expenses

voice_notes: Research-backed debunking posts work well — combining personal testing with academic findings creates credible counternarratives
Leading with specific failed examples before the broader analysis makes the critique more concrete
The 'sweet spot' framing works well — identifying the specific gap between Firebase and AWS helps readers understand the positioning problem
The 'trap' framing works well for operational problems — 'free tier trap' immediately conveys the hidden danger
Personal workflow audits add credibility to broader industry observations
Leading with a specific tool discovery (Toolspend) grounds abstract cost problems in concrete reality
Leading with a specific cost underestimation statistic (40-60%) immediately establishes the scale of the problem
The 'blind spot' framing works better than 'mistake' — it implies systemic issues rather than user error
